title: The Andalusī merchants of the crown complain about the privileges still held by the Catalan merchants of the Ṭāʾifa of Aragon. Their complaints are ignored
The trade wars escalate in the western Mediterranean: leaned on by the Angevins, Genoa embargoes Andalusī merchants in Italy. Al-Andalus answers by closing its ports to Angevin merchants

data.embargoBy: Genoa, under Angevin pressure, against al-Andalus
data.reply: al-Andalus embargoes the Angevin Empire's merchants in its ports

title: The Emperor wishes to restore Madīnat al-Zahrāʾ, the palace-city of the caliphs on the western edge of Qurṭuba, lost in the fitna of the eleventh century, to set himself above every ruler and pretender who might challenge him

options: They will see our prestige! (starts a Madīna az-Zahrāʾ building in Qurṭuba; costs 117 gold)
